prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B066 as a single-topic prize for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Round 1 sharpened rather than weakened the case. Three members independently describe the same principle, induced proximity, in which a small molecule becomes an adaptor between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, and all three name the same three laureates. The principle has a physical statement (a ternary complex whose formation and lifetime set degradation rates), it is reproduced by many independent groups, and it creates a capability occupancy-based inhibitors lack, namely acting on targets without an occupiable active site. That is the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' test I apply as Chair. On the one point I left open in round 1, I now keep Handa rather than Ciulli: cereblon is the shared receptor on which both strands rest, since it explains the thalidomide-type glues and is also the ligase most degrader programmes recruit, so Handa lets one citation cover glues and PROTACs without suggesting two prizes.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, so we would honour a mechanism and a platform before the clinical verdict, and Chabes may be right that it is a year or a few years early. Three names exclude Ciulli (VHL ligands and structures), Sakamoto and Kim (the first PROTAC), Gray and Ito, each with a defensible claim, and Handa's cereblon work is a glue discovery rather than the PROTAC concept, so Crews, Deshaies and Handa give an uneven split of the two strands. By contrast B038 and B057 are fully mature, and a committee that weights overdue recognition over early recognition could reasonably prefer them.

responses.point: Somfai argues that B038 has an unambiguous pair, Buchwald and Hartwig, a thirty-year record, and ligand design that makes a hard transformation routine, with 2010 as the main objection.
responses.response: This is the strongest alternative and I keep B038 as my first. You did not answer my round-1 question about what C-N coupling enabled that the 2010 prize did not. The answer I can accept is that the 2010 citation concerned C-C bond formation, while forming aryl C-N bonds with amines, which bind and poison palladium, needed a different ligand design and a different reductive-elimination problem, and that this unlocked whole classes of drugs and materials. I still see this as a major extension of a recognised framework rather than a new principle, and the Kosugi precursor has to be handled in the citation text or the discussion. That keeps B038 an alternative; it does not yet outweigh the new-capability argument for B066.

responses.point: Chabes says B066 may be one or a few years early because no degrader is approved, yet weighs heavily that the mechanism is reproduced by many independent groups, and he prefers B057 as his alternative.
responses.response: Your reproducibility criterion is the one I find most persuasive and it is what separates this case from a prize on hope. If ternary-complex structures and cereblon biochemistry have been independently reproduced, the science is secure and only the pharmacology is pending. I do not want to push a committee that I chair into a prize that ages badly, so I agree that the citation should avoid any claim about patient benefit and rest on the mechanism and its use as a research tool. I part from you on the B057 alternative: I keep it second, because I still need a sharper statement of the chemical invention before I would put it ahead of degradation.

responses.point: Aili holds that the modality shift from occupancy to event-driven pharmacology is chemical validation enough, and that thalidomide-type glues already in medical use make the chemistry mature even if PROTAC approvals lag.
responses.response: I agree and I use that argument too, but I would not lean on the medical use of thalidomide analogues, because that history overlaps with Medicine-type recognition and invites the objection that the clinical record is carrying the case. I would ground maturity in the structural and mechanistic work. I also share your concern, stated in your own uncertainties, about whether three names can fairly exclude Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim. My answer is that no three-person prize on this topic escapes an exclusion, and the committee should pick the three that anchor the concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the mechanism of the glue strand (Handa), which is the line of argument that is easiest to defend.

responses.point: Zou's top choice is B038, but he asks whether protein degradation can be given a clean attribution by the final ballot and notes that B038 may lack the breadth of support for five votes.
responses.response: My answer on attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional concept and Handa identified the ligase target of the glues, so each name maps onto a distinct, citable step. I take your point that a method may struggle to reach five, and I would be glad to know whether you can move to B066 as a second choice if B038 cannot carry. In return, if the group instead consolidates on B038, I would not block it, since the attribution is cleaner than for B066.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept recognition before the first approved degrader, which is the main risk for B066.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the right third name; I have settled on Handa but see it as a judgement call that Aqvist may contest.
Whether C-N coupling is judged distinct from the 2010 prize, which decides how strong B038 is as a fallback.
Whether B057 can be stated as a specific chemical invention rather than platform technology, and whether a third name is needed.
I did not move to a two-part prize: with the three-name cap I could not find a second part that others support enough to justify diluting a clean single citation.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need. I have no tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Buchwald, Hartwig or any other shortlisted name. I am a Lund colleague of Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, which does not touch any candidate. My nanowire and thermoelectric work is unrelated to B066.
